newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Ceval says sold soybeans to U.S. firm.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Ceval says sold soybeans to U.S. firm.

text.p: Brazilian processor Ceval Alimentos has sold 50,000 tonnes soybeans to a U.S. firm for May shipment, a company official said.
"Until now we have closed a deal for 50,000 tonnes soybeans for shipment in May," Charles Van Der Heyde, director of external trade at Ceval, told Reuters.
Ceval earlier this week said it was in talks to sell 230,000 tonnes soybeans and 150,000 tonnes soymeal to two separate U.S. firms for 15 April-30 May shipment.

Van Der Heyde said he could not disclose a price or the name of the buyer of the soybean cargo, but said the beans were heading for the U.S. Gulf and the deal was closed on Wednesday. On Monday, Ceval's offer stood at $307 FOB Brazil for the beans.
"We are negotiating some more soybeans for shipment in June," he said.
No deal has been reached on the soymeal sale which Ceval was offering for $300 FOB Monday. "We remained $4 apart," he said.
